reviews.text: The app is insanely buggy. From onboarding on, it’s been inventing stats that don’t match Screen Time in iOS settings (and I don’t know why it even thinks it’s useful to show a “trend” 37 minutes after download). On top of that, the block lists are unreliable: sometimes Reddit is blocked as a social app, other times it’s not; sometimes Messages is blocked despite being marked Allow. The whole thing reeks of style without substance.

reviews.title: Helpful, but annoying

I got so mad I deleted and cancelled the subscription. I loved the strict app blocking but there’s not even a FAQ section. Poor design in my mind. I also hated how it called things time wasters that weren’t. For example, I have a focus music app I use a lot, Opal has this big frame that’s calculating how much time I wasted listening to it and what I could have done instead… when it’s literally the kind of app you put on while you’re doing useful things. I think I can get a more striaghtforward app blocker that’s more user friendly, and probably less expensive.

reviews.title: Buggy Mess with horrible Support and a Scam

Then I got charged the yearly renewal which I imperially went to cancel and try to get a refund for. However despite the support page saying to contact their email they never responded and instead cancelled my pro membership instead, without first even giving the refund or ever contacting me back. Overall this app and company are horrible with a buggy mess of an app. They are many better, free alternatives. I highly recommend skipping on Opal. Just keep in mind if you ever feel like buying the subscription in a few months you may not even be able to use the app anymore.

reviews.title: Poor feedback / contact
reviews.text:
I actually do appreciate Opal, in general. It’s definitely helped me cut down on screentime. Was disappointed tho, that they’re taking the typical bogus approach to customer service by making themselves as unreachable to customers as possible. All I wanted was to send a quick message to the design team, and got stuck in some loop of community forums. I am not wasting my time on that BS. Seems rather ironic that a company claiming to help keep people off their screens would add layers of app garbage for what could just be a simple contact form— click and send. Disappointing. 

And all I had to say, as feedback, was that the backdrop has switched to an ocean scene, but it’s clearly something like AI. The sound doesn’t align with the scene, and it’s clearly a split screen-the same waves mirrored on both sides. Believe me, your customers do spend enough time in nature to know the difference between real ocean and fake. And I will not support AI in any way shape or form, so if this continues, you’ll have lost me. 

There’s also no way to mute the fake ocean sounds. If I’m checking my apps in public, I don’t need extra noise. Design a way to permanently mute the sounds in settings. And don’t waste our time with useless customer service blocks. It just tells me you’re eating up over $100 a year without wanting to actually serve your customers.

reviews.title: I miss the old Opal
reviews.text:
I don’t ever write reviews, but I just want to say when I found opal it was the best app I’ve ever downloaded. It was perfect for screen time monitoring and blocking. It used to be very easy to use and navigate. You used to be able to organize your apps by least to most distracting and also remove certain apps like Navigation/GPS or Music from your screen time. 

Now, everything is counted in your screen time, and even if I’m not using an app but it’s running in the background, like Life360, it counts that as screen time, which, sorry, is kind of absurd. I’m obviously not scrolling on life360 for fourteen hours. 

Also, since the big Opal update a few weeks or months back, certain features just haven’t been working as they used to, and the interface is much more confusing. Sometimes my gems don’t show up on the Home Screen— it’s just empty. For a few days my streak was set back to zero (which was fixed). The app is much more laggy now and sometimes crashes when I try to open it or when I try to unblock an app temporarily. 

One more thing— if you have a time limit rule for an app, say you set YouTube to be allowed for an hour a day, it seems that Opal just counts down from the time that you open the app now rather than monitoring when you’re on or off the app. I personally set my YouTube for 30 mins on certain days, and even if I just open it, watch a video, and exit the app, I’ll still get a notification a half hour later saying that it’s blocked again. 

There’s also a bug

reviews.title: Working hours are great but time keeping doesn’t work at all
reviews.text:
I like how I can block certain hours, helps me keep focus and eventually forget about the apps and focus on other tasks.

But the timekeeper doesn’t work at all. It will count I ‘hit my set limit) (1 hour) randomly in the middle of the night or anytime I’m not on my mobile. I check my ios screentime settings and I’ve only used apps for 30 minutes total.

This is extremely frustrating as I have the apps on my phone for a reason as a creator (otherwise I would just delete social media and call it a day) 

So when I need to upload content/reply to messages etc I cannot without manually unblocking for the day or resetting my limit, which defeats the purpose of having a set limit to begin with!

The app simply intended for timekeeping, its most basic functionality should not be this wrong.

The app itself also has pretty poor UI. It’s slow, laggy and adding/remove rules is very difficult. The app only does a few things, it doesn’t require so many windows and tabs.

When its doing the job of blocking, works great, my screentime has dropped massively but outside of that it really needs help.

reviews.title: Great App, Terrible Redesign
reviews.text:
I originally loved Opal because it helped me stay focused and reduce the impact of today’s increasingly addictive digital culture. Its App UI was not well designed but it worked. As an entrepreneur, it became an important part of my daily routine.
Unfortunately, the recent redesign has been incredibly disappointing. Users were given no meaningful warning, no transition period, and no option to continue using the previous interface while adapting to the new one. Instead, loyal customers were forced into an entirely unfamiliar experience overnight.
The new UI feels visually overwhelming and unnecessarily complicated. I don’t need stories, gems, or additional layers of gamification—I simply need clear, reliable controls to block distracting apps and reclaim my attention.
What’s most frustrating is that this change appears to ignore basic human-centered design principles. Major product changes should be introduced thoughtfully, with communication, onboarding, and user choice. Instead, users are expected to relearn everything immediately, with no direct feedback channel beyond a forum.
After years of enjoying and recommending Opal, I will not be renewing my subscription. I sincerely hope Apple or another company provides a simpler, more user-focused alternative for managing screen time and digital well-being.

Frankly this is shocking.

reviews.title: Charged me even after I canceled my subscription
reviews.text: i had used Opal in the past and redownloaded it again. it offered me another free trial ig cuz it's been long enough, so i think okay whatever i'll do that. it says it will remind me before my trial is up, but it didn't matter since i just went ahead and canceled it before the trial was over with. it asked me for my card info, yes, but it didn't say it would charge 99$ and it stated that it was only to pay after my trail was up. the charge of 99$ went through despite me canceling the free trial before the ending date, and now i can't download any apps cuz Apple thinks i'm bad with my money. i've tried emailing, no response. and ofc i the only other way to get in contact is through the app, but i can't download any apps! contacted Apple support and they also said that i needed to talk to Opal, not them. i really did love Opal a few years ago, and it helped for a long time and i was paying for the student version. but now it seems like this app is greedy and wants to screw users over. really disappointing since a few years ago i got tons of my friends to use it cuz i said i really loved it.

reviews.title: Too many bugs
reviews.text:
Update - Received a developer response to my review on a temporary fix while the resolve the issue. The issue is now happening daily, and I do not have the time or desire to go through the annoying process of deleting and redoing my app time limits. A bit ridiculous that they have been aware of the issue for weeks and still don’t have a solve. Considering deleting this app completely and moving onto someone else.

Have been using for over a month and great concept, but too may glitches makes the app extremely frustrating. Occasionally, the app won’t block apps that i’ve reached my limit for. It also frequently blocks apps that I have not even used yet at all! “Reloading blocks” does nothing at all. Lastly, I feel the screen time numbers may not be accurate. For example in the weekly summary, it stated yesterday i only used for less than 4 hours. I know for a fact that my screen time yesterday was over 5 hours, and can see that data elsewhere in the app that it was 5h15 mins. Almost like they’re skewing your data to make it look like the app is “helping” you more. Really hope these get fixed soon or i’ll be uninstalling.

reviews.title: Was great until it stopped working
reviews.text:
I was using the free version of this app and honestly it was really great and it offered more than enough to support me in reducing my screen time. 

Then one day it started to glitch and I haven’t got it to work properly since. For some reason the app will claim I’ve gone over my time limit on all the apps, all at the same time, usually after I’ve finish a schedule slot. My daily schedule was 9-5 and I would usually have a few breaks in between which would work fine but not the app claims I’ve exceeded my limit when I know for a fact I haven’t. The reload block function doesn’t work either, I have to go manually reset the limit for each one but besides that just means I’m adding to my overall screen time and it isn’t calculating based on the limit I’ve set.

I’ve tried deleting and reinstalling, I’ve tried deleting my limits and schedules too but still didn’t work. I’ve had to use another app now even though I was genuinely thinking about paying for is premium services. It was great when it worked but it just isn’t working.

reviews.title: Gross AI art and unwelcome noises
reviews.text:
This was a good and very chill healthy app. 
SO DID YOU REMOVE THE AI ART? ITS GROSS.. Recent updates have gone against the ethos. What was previously a mindfulness breathing exercise type page used before you take a break to use distracting apps is now a flash fast slideshow of disgusting generative AI art. Devs have stopped responding or acknowledging bugs. This audio playing while you wait function is poorly thought through and ruins the design of the app. The app also doesn’t remember if you’ve muted audio and so next time you take a break it may randomly spew out the audio selected by the app at that moment.. the mute button being on the screen close to the take a break/never mind is annoying as a third option you may accidentally touch while you wait. The developer claims to have fixed audio unmuting but it isn’t fixed and there should be a setting to completely remove this part of the app.

reviews.title: Nothing Special, Way Too Many Useless Features
reviews.text:
Is it a collecting rock and gems mini-game of a focus / productivity app? It's a focus app, but the gemstones take up about 50% of my home page when I open the app, how distracting for a focus app. Why is that even a thing? Not to mention you need to pay to fully block access to those apps completely, otherwise you can just ignore.. Focus section is pretty useless as well, if you have any self-control, you can sit your phone down, and not doomscroll while working. Apples system is honestly superior with much less features. I see nothing special, just a lot of random features thrown in to an app. Such as the gemstones, streaks, the whole home screen, there's a lot of useless things in the app, every page. As a young adult with self control (most of the time), who limits social media to 1 hour a day, this app does very little for me, except give me gemstones to collect! 
Giving it 2 star because it at least has some good features in PRO. Although would be a 1 star if PRO version didn't exist, since it would be reductant compared to Apples.
